region: San Bartolomé · Lanzarote, Canary Islands, Spain
about: Lanzarote is the easternmost of the Canary Islands, about 125 kilometres off the coast of Africa, and between 1730 and 1736 a series of eruptions buried much of it under three to five metres of lava and ash. Bodegas Los Bermejos was founded in 2001 beside an 18th-century manor house in San Bartolomé, in the island’s centre, and is run by partner and winemaker Ignacio Valdera. Alongside its own vines it works with hundreds of small growers who farm this unlikely landscape.

Vineyards here look like nowhere else. Each vine sits in its own hoyo, a hollow dug through the black volcanic ash to reach the older soil below, sheltered by a crescent of stone against the constant trade winds. The ash holds what little rain falls, the old vines are ungrafted, and yields are tiny. Malvasía Volcánica, the island’s signature grape, is a native crossing of Malvasía Aromática and Marmajuelo. The grapes are pressed very gently as whole clusters, fermented cool in tank and aged on their lees, with no oak.

The dry Malvasía is the winery’s flagship, making up well over half of what it produces. Crisp and bright, it carries citrus, lemon and mango, citrus zest and peach skin over a deep mineral core. Critic John Gilman scored the 2024 93 points, describing lime, pear and passion fruit, wild fennel and white flowers over a distinctly volcanic minerality, and gave it a drinking window running past 2035.
facts: Ungrafted vines planted in hoyos (hollows) in volcanic ash
Gentle whole-cluster pressing; temperature-controlled fermentation in tank
On the lees in stainless steel; no oak
Sustainable, all by hand; some cuvées certified organic depending on vintage

awards.by: John Gilman, View from the Cellar
